text: You stay sealed off long after the reason has gone. Needing no one once kept you safe, and you still shut out help without checking whether you want any. Remember that you meant to keep out the hurt and never the people near you.

Being nobody's burden is why you ask no one. You would rather owe nothing than share the load, and you take the job back the moment someone offers. You send away the person who offered and leave them no way to help you.

Being hard on yourself is a rule you never had to learn. Every standard turns into a judge in you, and you would rather fail your own hard test than pass someone else's easy one. You answer to no judge harder than yourself.

Being wrong is what you have no procedure for. Right answers feel like the only safe ones, and you hold opinions back rather than risk a mistake. You lose every idea you kept back for fear of being wrong.

Hating being wrong is the part of you that works hardest. A mistake feels like a mark on your name, and you give silence in place of any answer that risks being wrong. You go silent on the answers you had right.

Having earned your own place, you check that everyone who rises near you earned theirs. An unearned rank looks wrong to you, and you credit people for the record more than the talent. Bright newcomers wait a long time for your nod.

Spending it all feels like generosity to you. You spend it on the bill, the gift and the loan, since giving suits you better than keeping. You meant to make the people you love feel rich, and you leave them short for later.

Holding on tight makes what you have feel safe. You would rather keep a thing than risk losing it, and you grip money, things and people past where holding helps. You have every right to let go of what you no longer want.
Where you feel surest is starting fast. You start on speed alone, and your patience runs out somewhere in the middle. The payday sits at the end of the work, long after your attention has moved on.

You hand people your read in its plainest, most direct form. Plain truth feels like respect to you, and you cut the kind words and keep only the point. You leave them a bruise the truth alone would not have left.

Being exact costs you people who talk loosely. You correct a small error in a story rather than let it land, and over time fewer people tell you much. You wanted to be told more than you wanted it exact.

Your door stays closed while you stay the student. You keep learning under someone else's wing instead of spreading your own, and the people who need your shelter wait outside. Each year you remain the student is a year they go without it.

You are hard to reach while a thought is unfinished, and most of yours are. Finishing the thought comes before answering the message, and the person waiting hears nothing for days. You leave them with less of you than they came for.

Anything hard that has to reach someone, you warm first. Softening it feels kinder to you than saying it straight, and the plain version stays behind the comfort. Bad news from you lands softly, and nobody feels small hearing it.
Every race you love needs someone else in it. You make a rival of a peer without asking first, and the race starts on your word. Time with you comes with a scoreboard running.

You give your hours to whoever is nearest, without deciding. Saying yes to everyone is easier than choosing, and the few counting on you get what is left. You give away to everyone the hours meant for the few.

With whoever is in charge, you pick fights as your own kind of honesty. Because you fight in public rather than private, you cost the one above you their footing in front of others. You leave them no quiet way to answer you.

To stay honest with people, you share everything you think. You say it all before asking how much they want, and they get no choice in what they carry. You spend their attention on more of your thinking than they asked for.

Mocking is your first language, and plain praise comes out like a foreign one. Since being clever feels safer than being seen caring, you mock what you love instead of praising it. You mean the fondness far more than the mocking lets on.

Waiting for permission keeps you in line. Since permission given feels cleaner than permission taken, you would rather keep your place than claim the next one. You watch the step above yours go to whoever stopped waiting first.

Managing without asking is what you do best. Owing anyone feels worse to you than the work, and you choose doing it alone rather than asking for company. You miss out on the ease that help would have given you.

Staying in is how you avoid being tested. Feeling unready is easier to live with than failing, and you stay long past the day leaving was open to you. You are allowed to be tested and come home again.
Spending shared money comes easier to you than spending your own. Nobody's name is on it, and you dip into it before asking who put what in. You run the pool down faster than anyone agreed to.

Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Metal makes it hard, and your will holds. Running thin, your strength gives out sooner than you let on. You spend it as if it were full and seldom stop to refill.
no_change_reason: "sooner than" here means time: your strength gives out earlier than you admit, not "rather than". Kept as it is.
